_note: TEST config: the real config with the fixture anchor and scope.
_decided_by: DRAFT — pending Ashwin S Thankachan's approval at gate G2/G4 (see logs/runs)

anchor._why: My target occupation: new-grad backend software engineer = O*NET 15-1252.00 Software Developers. Every other occupation is compared with it.

scope._why: Only O*NET major group 15 (Computer and Mathematical) counts as a candidate occupation for a software posting. Matches outside it (e.g. 'Full Stack Developer' under 51-9151.00 Photographic Process Workers) are reported as ignored, never scored.

distinguishable._why: Two pivot scores are called different only if they differ by more than z standard errors of the difference. 1.96 is the usual 95% two-sided cutoff. The standard error assumes the nine O*NET ratings' errors are independent — they are probably positively correlated, which makes the true error larger, so this rule is generous to differences.

dated_ratings._why: Flag a comparison when the two occupations' ratings were made this many years apart or more (O*NET 'Date' column). 5 years separates pre- and post-LLM-coding-tool ratings for most pairs.

title_normalization._why: Words removed from a posting title before looking it up in O*NET's title lists. Level and location words don't change the occupation.

families._why: Fallback ONLY when O*NET has no exact title match: a title rule (regex) puts the posting in a family, and the family's canonical titles are looked up in O*NET instead. The canonical titles are my choice, so a fallback match is labelled your-input, not record. First matching family wins.

pins._why: A human's one-occupation choice for a normalized title, made at gate G2 when the candidates disagree. Empty until I pin something; each pin needs a reason.

posting_signal._why: Which sentences in a posting's responsibilities read as system-judgment / verification work (the Cognitive Pivot thesis) versus routine implementation. A sentence with any judgment phrase counts as judgment; a sentence with only routine phrases counts as routine. Fewer than min_sentences classified sentences = 'too few signals', never zero.
posting_signal.section_start_re: ^(what you('|’)?ll do|what you will do|responsibilities|key responsibilities|in this role|the role|your impact|what you('|’)?ll be doing|day[- ]to[- ]day|about the role|you will|what you('|’)?ll work on)\b
posting_signal.section_end_re: ^(what you('|’)?ll bring|what you bring|qualifications|requirements|minimum qualifications|preferred qualifications|who you are|about you|you have|you might be|nice to have|bonus|benefits|compensation|pay|salary|perks|why join|about us|about the team)\b

liveness._why: Liveness is a GATE. A board-API listing is open at its fetched_at time only. Older than this many days → CHECK-LIVENESS. Shortlisted postings are re-checked with the repo's npm run ats:liveness, whose saved output overrides the listing.

fetch._why: Which public Greenhouse boards to read and which postings count as backend-adjacent. Boston-area employers (the first nine are the boards from my Recipe Design sweep; CarGurus and Datadog added 2026-10-20 after checking they answer). Seniority is NOT filtered: this mode is about the kind of work, not the level.
